title: Functions and constants are class members; `Core` is the reserved namespace for built-ins
scope:
where a `function` or a `const` may be declared; the reserved `Core` namespace and its
domain-class shape; how PHP's global functions and global constants are organised as built-ins

summary.headline: Every function and constant is a class member; built-ins live under `Core`
summary.body:
A `function` or `const` declared outside a class does not compile. PHP's global functions and
constants are instead static members of classes in a reserved `Core` namespace, grouped by
domain: `strlen($s)` becomes `Core\Str::length($s)`, and `PHP_EOL` becomes `Core\Env::EOL`.
Nothing under `Core` is imported for you; you write `use Core\Str;` as for any other namespace.
Anonymous and arrow functions are values, not declarations, and are unaffected. The cost falls
on converted PHP code, where every built-in call is renamed; the gain is that no bare name is
ever resolved by a fallback.
